subject: Lightning.ai pilot: latency thresholds & hosting mode recommendation
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Reddy <priya.reddy@lightning.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-06-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Recap + next steps from today — latency/throughput targets and hosting options

Hi Priya — thanks again for a productive call this morning. Short recap + a couple quick asks so we can size the pilot and recommend a deployment path (Hosted vs Dedicated).

Key signals from the call:
- Desired production P50 latency: <= 40ms (text generation, 512 tokens)
- Desired production P95 latency target: <= 120ms (hard requirement for UI flows)
- Sustained QPS target: ~350–450 qps during daytime traffic; expected burst windows up to ~1,200 qps for 10–20 minute spikes
- Model family: open-architecture transformer, ~30B parameters (we discussed quantized variants)
- Compliance: SOC 2 required, possible customer audit in H2

Open / asks for you to confirm:
1) Is the burst profile bursty (short spikes as above) or more prolonged (30+ minutes)?
2) Any data residency constraints beyond US?
3) Do you have a hard preference for Dedicated (reserved GPU pools) for production or would you consider starting on Hosted API for the functional pilot and moving to Dedicated for production?

Attached: pilot_scope.pdf (draft scope + telemetry we need).

Proposed next steps from our side once you confirm the three items above:
- Engineering: quick benchmark plan for a hosted pilot (3–5 days) to validate functional latency under sample traffic
- Ops: Dedicated capacity sizing + ballpark pricing for the steady-state and autoscale strategy (if you want production Dedicated)
- Security: intake of SOC2/GDPR items (we can share our evidence pack)

Suggest a 30-min follow-up next week to finalize the pilot path — I can do Tue/Wed morning PT.

Best,
Logan Wright
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Priya Reddy <priya.reddy@lightning.ai>

Cc:   
Date: 2028-06-01T11:06:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Recap + next steps from today — latency/throughput targets and hosting options

Thanks, Logan — great summary. Confirming a few points and adding context:

- Burst profile: mostly short spikes (5–25 minutes), aligned with product launches and end-of-hour batch finishes. We have seen a handful of longer bursts but those are exceptions.
- Sustained qps: plan for 350 qps as the baseline, with capacity for bursts to 1,200 qps as you outlined.
- Latency tolerance: P95 <= 150ms is acceptable if P50 stays ~40ms; the UI team will tolerate a slightly wider P95 during bursts.
- Compliance: SOC2 Type II required before GA; happy to start pilot while you provide SOC artifacts.

Regarding hosting preference: our platform team prefers Dedicated for production (predictable performance and auditability). That said, we would consider a Hosted pilot for a faster functional validation if the migration path and data handling are clear.

I've attached our security intake questionnaire — can you confirm which fields you need answered vs. which we can cover during a security review call?

Thanks — Priya
Priya Reddy
Director of Product, Lightning.ai
priya.reddy@lightning.ai

From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc:   
Date: 2028-06-02T08:42:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: Lightning.ai — recommended two-track pilot (hosted -> dedicated) + asks for ops/price

Team — looping you in with confirmed numbers from Priya. Proposal: offer a two-track pilot to accelerate time-to-first-value while keeping the Dedicated path clear for production.

Proposal outline (internal):
1) Hosted pilot (30 days):
   - Purpose: functional validation, instrumentation, and end-to-end latency profile under their real request shapes
   - Goals: validate P50 <= 40ms, measure prefix cache hit rates, identify batching opportunities
   - Data handling: ensure no customer PII sent during pilot or use redaction; provide SOC artifacts as requested
2) Dedicated production plan:
   - Purpose: predictable P95/SLO and auditability for GA
   - Scaling: autoscale policy with warm pool for burst handling (we discussed warm pool for 2x burst headroom)

Immediate asks for pricing and infra team (Ben / Marissa):
- Ballpark Dedicated sizing for 350 sustained qps / 1,200 qps bursts and expected latency envelope (P50/P95) using our 30B quantized model variant- Cost ranges for: steady reserved pool + optional burst capacity billable by minute- Recommended autoscale warm-pool config and expected spin-up time
- Any quick optimizations (prefix/KV caching, aggressive batching, quantized model variant) we should propose to Priya to reduce cost while meeting latencies

I want to include a draft pricing file and an operations runbook in my reply to Priya tomorrow.

Thanks — Logan
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc:   
Date: 2028-06-03T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Internal: Lightning.ai — recommended two-track pilot (hosted -> dedicated) + asks for ops/price

Ack. Notes from sizing side (ballpark):

Sizing assumption: 30B model (quantized int8 variant), average request ~512 tokens, steady-state 350 qps, burst 1,200 qps.

Dedicated recommendation (steady + burst headroom):
- Steady pool: 4x vGPU nodes (A100-equivalent or next-gen), each node ~100 qps sustained with low-p95; this gives ~400 qps steady with redundancy
- Warm pool / burst capacity: additional 2x nodes in warm state, autoscale to +4 nodes during sustained bursts; target spin-up <2 minutes with pre-warmed caches
- Expected latencies: P50 ~35–45ms, P95 ~90–140ms depending on cache hit-rate and batching (we should plan for the higher end during full-burst scenarios)

Cost (very rough):
- Reserved steady pool (4 nodes): $XXk/mo (I'll insert exact pricing in the attached draft)
- Burst minutes billed per-minute for additional nodes (configurable caps)

Optimizations to propose to Lightning.ai:
- KV prefix caching for repeated session prompts (can drop effective token compute >30% for many flows)
- Aggressive micro-batching for background calls (not UI critical)
- Offer quantized model variant for production if Lightning accepts tiny accuracy tradeoffs

Attaching draft_pricing_sheet.csv with a simple reserved + burst pricing model so Logan can share a ballpark.

Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai

Subject: Proposal: 30-day hosted pilot + Dedicated production path — proposed next steps

Hi Priya — thanks for the quick confirmation earlier. Based on Ben's sizing notes I attached a ballpark pricing sheet to give you a sense of committed vs burst economics.

Proposed next steps (short list):
- Lightning next action: sign-off on pilot traffic shape and confirm any PII exclusions (response requested by 2028-06-07)
- Redwood action: schedule 30-day hosted pilot (engineering kick on 2028-06-12), share SOC2 artifacts, and enable telemetry dashboard
- Joint call: review Dedicated sizing and pricing (45 minutes) — suggested slot: 2028-06-13 10:00–10:45 PT or 2028-06-14 08:00–08:45 PT. Which works better for your team?
- Security: plan a 60-min intake with our security lead the week of 2028-06-19 to go over the questionnaire answers

If you prefer to jump straight to Dedicated for the pilot, we can provide an accelerated Dedicated onboarding (adds ~5 business days for provisioning). Either approach is supported — the two-track flow just reduces initial risk and time-to-insight.

Please confirm preferred meeting time and whether we should provision Hosted pilot or straight-to-Dedicated.
